Rather than treating memory as a primitive, it derives persistence as the structural object forced whenever bounded observers repeatedly evaluate admissible states under a declared regime. A definitional impossibility argument (the Recurrence Lemma) shows that, absent recurrence, persistence is not distinguishable from storage as a separate operation. Persistence is therefore derived as the prerequisite for memory, which is interpreted as one realization of persistence—specifically replay—alongside regeneration, reconstruction, equilibrium restoration, and constraint re-satisfaction.
